Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.
requirements.acceptance: The imported Training Dummy sits at a fixed CFrame with no Humanoid health depletion, no flinch/reactive animation, and no movement or attack behavior; any embedded script that would add such behavior is disabled/excluded after inspection.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

requirements.description: A plain, undecorated flat floor holds the fixed dummy placement point and a spawn point a short walk away, with no arena decoration or props.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then

		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

Runs an infinite while-true loop (wait(0)) polling script.Parent.Humanoid.Health; if Health<1 it waits 1s, clones the stored original, parents the clone to script.Parent.Parent, calls makeJoints() on it, then removes the original dummy Model. No animation/movement/attack logic; purely a death-respawn watcher tied to the dummy's own Humanoid health.

requirements.reason: Geometry (Parts/Mesh/Head/Torso/Decal) is a stationary, non-humanoid-controlled prop with a fixed CFrame achievable by placement, satisfying most of this requirement. The Model provides distinguishable body parts (e.g. Torso, Head) usable as a hitbox reference, but no source in this component defines or wires a hitbox for server-side overlap/distance checks; that logic is owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task and is not present in this captured asset.

integrationNotes: Disable or remove the 'Respawn' Script (index 18) before placing the dummy so no death/respawn behavior can ever trigger, satisfying the non-reactive stationary requirement; this removal is a proposed integration action, not yet applied.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Keep this minimal: the default player avatar, selected stationary dummy, one punch action with its animation, successful-hit sound, and hit counter. Use a plain floor and the default Roblox camera. Remove the reset-counter control, dummy flinch, arena decoration, movement restrictions, and custom clothing. The selected assets provide the appearance. Keep the counter for this play session. Preserve the selected assets and keep all three proposal sections consistent with these limits.

Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The selected training dummy asset (1245720733) is placed at a fixed point, has no health, cannot be damaged or knocked over, never attacks, and shows no flinch or reactive animation.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.
requirements.acceptance: The imported Training Dummy sits at a fixed CFrame with no Humanoid health depletion, no flinch/reactive animation, and no movement or attack behavior; any embedded script that would add such behavior is disabled/excluded after inspection.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Keep this minimal: the default player avatar, selected stationary dummy, one punch action with its animation, successful-hit sound, and hit counter. Use a plain floor and the default Roblox camera. Remove the reset-counter control, dummy flinch, arena decoration, movement restrictions, and custom clothing. The selected assets provide the appearance. Keep the counter for this play session. Preserve the selected assets and keep all three proposal sections consistent with these limits.

Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.

No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

Runs an infinite while-true loop (wait(0)) polling script.Parent.Humanoid.Health; if Health<1 it waits 1s, clones the stored original, parents the clone to script.Parent.Parent, calls makeJoints() on it, then removes the original dummy Model. No animation/movement/attack logic; purely a death-respawn watcher tied to the dummy's own Humanoid health.

requirements.reason: Geometry (Parts/Mesh/Head/Torso/Decal) is a stationary, non-humanoid-controlled prop with a fixed CFrame achievable by placement, satisfying most of this requirement. The Model provides distinguishable body parts (e.g. Torso, Head) usable as a hitbox reference, but no source in this component defines or wires a hitbox for server-side overlap/distance checks; that logic is owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task and is not present in this captured asset.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Keep this minimal: the default player avatar, selected stationary dummy, one punch action with its animation, successful-hit sound, and hit counter. Use a plain floor and the default Roblox camera. Remove the reset-counter control, dummy flinch, arena decoration, movement restrictions, and custom clothing. The selected assets provide the appearance. Keep the counter for this play session. Preserve the selected assets and keep all three proposal sections consistent with these limits.

Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.

The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

requirements.description: A plain, undecorated flat floor holds the fixed dummy placement point and a spawn point a short walk away, with no arena decoration or props.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.
requirements.acceptance: A single flat floor Part exists with no additional props or backdrop; the dummy sits at a fixed point and the spawn point is placed a short walk from it, with no invisible walls or boundary parts added.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then

		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

need.role: Stationary training dummy providing the target's appearance and hitbox for punch registration
need.constraints: Must resolve to the user-selected asset 1245720733 (Training Dummy by Xtrah962). Verify it is a stationary, non-humanoid-controlled prop with no health/damage/AI loop. Identify a clear hitbox part usable for server distance/overlap checks. Inspect its 1 embedded script and report/exclude any behavior that would move, flinch, or animate the dummy, since the approved design requires it to remain purely stationary and non-reactive.

intent.experienceRole: The sole punchable target that gives the player a concrete goal to walk to and strike; its fixed presence anchors the entire training-drill loop.
intent.interaction: Non-interactive prop for positioning purposes only; the player's punch strike-window overlaps its hitbox to register a hit server-side, but the dummy itself never reacts, moves, flinches, or attacks.
reusableFeatures: Existing red/black canvas heavy-bag mesh and stand/base geometry
A distinguishable torso/body part usable as the hit-detection hitbox
Inspection of the embedded script to confirm it does not add movement, damage, or AI behavior that must be disabled

need.role: R15-compatible forward jab punch animation clip for the player's avatar
need.constraints: Must resolve to the user-selected asset 12061946559 (R15 Punching Animations by Auevi). Locate the embedded clip at key 1/1/18/1 specifically. Verify R15 rig compatibility with the default Roblox avatar and a duration of roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds covering windup/strike/recovery. Extract a usable Animation/AnimationId reference for Animator playback. Report, rather than execute, any packaged behavior script unrelated to the animation data itself.

intent.experienceRole: Provides the core visual feedback that makes each punch read as a deliberate player action distinct from idle movement, central to the requested fighting-game feel.
intent.interaction: Played once per server-approved punch input, timed to the authoritative strike window; purely presentational and does not itself decide hit success.
reusableFeatures: The specific embedded clip at key 1/1/18/1
Any keyframe markers indicating strike-frame timing useful for syncing the server hit-check window
Confirmation of R15 Animator/AnimationController compatibility with the default avatar rig

need.role: Punch/hit impact sound effect played once per successful connect
need.constraints: Must resolve to the user-selected asset 132504023010884 (Punch Impact 1 by NickySergal). Verify it loads and plays correctly as a Sound instance parented near the dummy's hitbox, triggered server-side so playback replicates to the client. Confirm it is a short one-shot 'thwack'-style connect sound, not a whiff/miss variant, and pass load/playback/listening checks before acceptance.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers the auditory payoff confirming a successful hit, reinforcing the arcade-boxing 'thwack' feel called for in the approved theme.
intent.interaction: Plays exactly once per confirmed successful punch connection, synchronized with the hit-counter increment; not ambient or decorative audio.
reusableFeatures: The single verified one-shot audio clip
Any loudness/tone characteristics worth preserving for a satisfying impact feel

data.reason: Dummy geometry, mesh, head/torso parts and decal texture are reusable for appearance and hitbox placement, but the embedded 'Respawn' Script implements a health-death respawn loop that conflicts with the required purely stationary, non-reactive dummy and must be disabled/excluded before acceptance; that removal has not been applied yet.

serializedMedia.purpose: Decal texture on Torso providing the dummy's canvas heavy-bag visual appearance

sources.behavior: On load clones script.Parent (the dummy Model) into a local var. Runs an infinite while-true loop (wait(0)) polling script.Parent.Humanoid.Health; if Health<1 it waits 1s, clones the stored original, parents the clone to script.Parent.Parent, calls makeJoints() on it, then removes the original dummy Model. No animation/movement/attack logic; purely a death-respawn watcher tied to the dummy's own Humanoid health.

requirements.reason: Geometry (Parts/Mesh/Head/Torso/Decal) is a stationary, non-humanoid-controlled prop with a fixed CFrame achievable by placement, satisfying most of this requirement. However the embedded Respawn Script watches script.Parent.Humanoid.Health and would clone/respawn the dummy on death, which conflicts with 'no reactive behavior/cannot be defeated'; per the requirement's own acceptance criteria this script must be disabled/excluded, which has not yet been done.

The Model provides distinguishable body parts (e.g. Torso, Head) usable as a hitbox reference, but no source in this component defines or wires a hitbox for server-side overlap/distance checks; that logic is owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task and is not present in this captured asset.

integrationNotes: Disable or remove the 'Respawn' Script (index 18) before placing the dummy so no death/respawn behavior can ever trigger, satisfying the non-reactive stationary requirement; this removal is a proposed integration action, not yet applied.
Torso (index 15) is the most distinguishable body part suitable to designate as the server-side hit-detection hitbox for the pending hitDetectionModule work.
Decal Texture rbxassetid://406436910 on the Torso (index 16) supplies the dummy's canvas heavy-bag visual appearance and is reusable as-is for the requested gym theme.

Humanoid (index 17) remains present on the dummy; ensure no damage-dealing script is ever added elsewhere in the namespace, since even with the Respawn script disabled the dummy should never take or process damage per r_dummy_stationary.

plan.reason: The prior review flagged the embedded 'Respawn' Script (index 18) as unsafe/unsuitable behavior: it polls the dummy's own Humanoid.Health and, on death, clones and re-parents a fresh dummy while destroying the original. This directly conflicts with r_dummy_stationary's requirement that the dummy 'cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over' and shows no reactive behavior, and it is unrelated to any requested mechanic. This manifest removes only that Script subtree, preserving every other node: the Model hierarchy, its Parts, SpecialMesh geometry, Head, Torso, the Torso's Decal (rbxassetid://406436910 canvas heavy-bag texture), and the Humanoid component itself, which remains present but will never be driven by any damage-dealing logic elsewhere in this namespace. No replacement source or new script is added by this component; hitbox wiring and overlap math are explicitly owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task per the accepted integration task list, not by this asset-adaptation step.

removeSubtrees.reason: Embedded 'Respawn' Script implements a Humanoid-health-triggered clone/respawn loop that would make the dummy reactive to damage and eventually swap/destroy the original Model. This conflicts with r_dummy_stationary's explicit acceptance criteria (no health depletion, no reactive/respawn behavior, cannot be defeated) and has no requested role in this minimal training-drill scope. Removing it is safe: it is a leaf Script with no descendants, and no other captured node references or depends on it.

preservedBehavior: Model hierarchy (index 1-2) and all body Parts (indices 3,5,7,9,10,11,12) with their SpecialMesh geometry (indices 4,6,8) retained unchanged, preserving the dummy's red/black canvas heavy-bag visual shape.
Head (index 13) and its SpecialMesh (index 14) retained unchanged.
Torso (index 15) retained unchanged as the distinguishable body part designated for later hitbox use by the separate hitDetectionModule task.
Torso Decal (index 16) with Texture rbxassetid://406436910 retained unchanged, preserving the dummy's existing canvas heavy-bag appearance required by r_theme_gym.

Humanoid (index 17) retained on the Model; it remains present as part of the asset's original rig but is not wired to any damage source in this namespace, so it will not deplete or trigger reactive behavior now that the Respawn watcher script is removed.
All joints/welds implicit in the original Part hierarchy are left intact since no geometry-bearing node was altered or removed.
remainingIntegration: Placement of this dummy Model at the fixed world position/CFrame specified for the practice-dummy target is owned by the worldSetup/dummyAssetIntegration tasks, not this component-level edit.

Designating Torso (index 15) as the authoritative server-side hitbox reference and implementing the strike-window overlap/distance math is owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task; no hitbox-defining code exists in this captured component.

Ensuring no other script anywhere in the namespace ever calls TakeDamage/sets Health on this dummy's Humanoid must be verified during integration of PunchServer and HitDetectionModule, since the Humanoid component itself was preserved rather than removed.
Visual/theme acceptance of the decal texture and mesh geometry against r_theme_gym still requires native rendering verification once the dummy is placed in the scene; this was not performed here.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Keep this minimal: the default player avatar, selected stationary dummy, one punch action with its animation, successful-hit sound, and hit counter. Use a plain floor and the default Roblox camera. Remove the reset-counter control, dummy flinch, arena decoration, movement restrictions, and custom clothing. The selected assets provide the appearance. Keep the counter for this play session. Preserve the selected assets and keep all three proposal sections consistent with these limits.

Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.

A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.

Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

requirements.description: The full punch loop works end to end: pressing the single punch input while not mid-punch triggers a server-approved punch, plays the animation, checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy, and on success plays the sound and increments the counter.
requirements.sourceQuote: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing the punch input (left click / Space / gamepad A) while not mid-punch produces a full observable cycle: server approval, client animation playback, server hit-window check against the dummy, and on success a synchronized sound plus a +1 counter update, reproducible across repeated swings with correct cooldown gating.

requirements.description: The player cannot chain or spam punches: a punch action can only start if the player is not already mid-punch, and only one hit registers per swing even if dummy overlap persists across multiple frames.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player (default Roblox avatar) faces the selected stationary target dummy asset. Pressing a single 'Punch' input (default: left mouse click or gamepad face button A / keyboard Space) triggers a punch action if the player is not already mid-punch (no combo chaining). The punch action plays a forward jab animation lasting roughly 0.3-0.5 seconds (windup, strike, recovery). A hit is registered when the punch's active strike frame overlaps the dummy's hitbox. On a successful hit: (1) a punch/hit sound effect plays once, (2) the on-screen hit counter increments by exactly 1. A brief cooldown ensures only one hit is registered per punch swing, even if overlap persists across multiple frames. The dummy has no health, cannot be defeated, never attacks back, and shows no flinch or reactive animation. There is no reset-counter control; the counter persists for the play session and resets only on scene reload/restart. Player movement uses standard default Roblox movement controls (WASD/left stick) with no added arena boundaries or movement restrictions beyond the default playable space; no jumping or blocking mechanics are included in this scope.
Single-player only; no multiplayer, AI opponent behavior, or networking.
Dummy is purely stationary and cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over, and has no flinch or reactive animation.
Only one punch type/animation is required (no combos, kicks, blocks, or special moves) per the request scope.
Hit counter is a simple integer displayed as on-screen UI text (e.g., 'Hits: 0') anchored to a screen corner.
Counter increments exactly once per successful punch connection using a per-swing hit-registered flag.
Default control scheme: standard Roblox movement plus one button for punching; no reset-counter input or button is included.
No scoring, timer, win condition, or difficulty progression is required; this is a practice/demo loop.
Punch and hit use the same single sound effect (no separate whiff vs. connect sounds) unless later expanded.
Player avatar and dummy appearance are provided entirely by the selected default/selected Roblox assets; no custom clothing or rig modifications are required.
Camera uses the default Roblox third-person follow camera; no fixed framing or custom camera control is implemented.
requirements.acceptance: Server rejects a new RequestPunch while the player's per-player mid-punch/cooldown flag is true; a per-swing hit-registered flag ensures at most one hit is counted per swing regardless of how long strike-window overlap with the dummy lasts.

requirements.description: The scene reads as a lighthearted training-gym aesthetic using the selected dummy's existing red/black canvas styling and default bright Roblox lighting, with no added decoration.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A lighthearted training-gym aesthetic: the player is a boxer/martial artist in practice gear (tank top, wraps or gloves, shorts) working out in a no-frills gym corner. The target dummy is a classic red-and-black canvas heavy-bag-style humanoid dummy mounted on a weighted base, evoking boxing gyms and arcade punch-meter machines. Tone is upbeat and casual, not violent or gory — this is presented as a training/fitness minigame rather than a combat-to-defeat scenario, reinforced by the dummy's harmless flinch reaction and the absence of health bars or damage numbers. Sound design leans into satisfying 'thwack'/glove-impact punch sounds reminiscent of classic arcade boxing games. The on-screen hit counter is styled like a gym rep-counter or arcade score display (bold numerals, simple font) to reinforce the training-drill framing.
Visual tone is stylized/cartoonish rather than photorealistic or gory, keeping the experience family-friendly.
Player and dummy character models are generic/unbranded (no licensed characters or IP references).
Setting is a single indoor gym-style room; no outdoor or narrative story elements are needed.
No dialogue, voiceover, or narrative text is required beyond the hit counter UI.
Color palette and lighting are simple/bright (gym lighting) rather than dramatic or moody, matching the low-stakes training theme.
requirements.acceptance: The dummy's imported appearance plus default Lighting settings (no custom rigs) together present a bright, casual gym-training look with zero additional decorative props beyond the selected dummy asset.

requirements.description: A plain, undecorated flat floor holds the fixed dummy placement point and a spawn point a short walk away, with no arena decoration or props.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Layout is a plain flat floor with no additional decoration, props, or themed backdrop. The selected stationary target dummy asset is placed at a fixed point on the floor; the player spawns using the default Roblox avatar a short distance away, within comfortable punching range after a short walk. The on-screen hit counter UI is anchored to a fixed screen-space position (e.g., top-center or top-right) so it remains visible during gameplay. The scene uses the default Roblox camera (third-person follow) with no custom framing. There are no invisible walls, arena boundaries, or added movement restrictions; the player can move freely across the plain floor using standard default movement, relying on default Roblox physics and collision.
Single static scene; no level transitions, multiple rooms, or loading between areas.
Play space is a plain floor with no decorative props, backdrop, or themed environment art; only the selected dummy asset and default avatar are present.
Lighting uses Roblox default lighting; no custom or dynamic lighting rigs are configured.
No destructible or interactive environment props beyond the dummy itself in this scope.
No arena boundaries or invisible walls are added; player movement is unrestricted beyond the standard default playable area.
requirements.acceptance: A single flat floor Part exists with no additional props or backdrop; the dummy sits at a fixed point and the spawn point is placed a short walk from it, with no invisible walls or boundary parts added.

requirements.description: The server independently validates the requesting player's state (humanoid existence/health, current mid-punch/cooldown state) and distance to the dummy hitbox before approving a punch or registering a hit, never trusting client-supplied hit claims.
requirements.acceptance: PunchServer checks the requesting player's Humanoid, current cooldown/mid-punch flag, and distance/overlap against the dummy hitbox server-side before approving a punch or confirming a hit; no hit/miss/timestamp claim from the client is trusted directly.

requirements.description: The experience is single-player focused with no AI opponent behavior; if multiple players are present, each player's cooldown and hit count are tracked independently.
requirements.acceptance: No AI opponent, PvP, or cross-player interference exists; per-player cooldown state and hit counts are keyed by UserId so concurrent players do not affect each other's counters.

requirements.description: Per-player server state and client-side connections are cleaned up and rebound correctly on player leave and character respawn, avoiding stale state or duplicate HUDs.
requirements.acceptance: On PlayerRemoving, the player's cooldown state and hit-count entry are removed from server tables; on CharacterAdded, the client's input/animation controller and HUD rebind to the new character without duplicating connections or creating a stale duplicate counter display.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: Three Marketplace assets were already selected by the user and must be preserved and integrated rather than replaced: (1) 'Training Dummy' (1245720733) supplies the stationary target's full appearance and geometry - its single embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep or disable it, since the requirement is a purely stationary, non-reactive dummy; (2) 'R15 Punching Animations' (12061946559) supplies the forward jab clip at embedded key 1/1/18/1, which must be located, verified as R15-compatible with the default avatar, and exposed for Animator playback - per the standalone-animation limitation, this is sourced as a Model pack rather than a bare Animation asset; (3) 'Punch Impact 1' (132504023010884) supplies the one-shot hit sound, which must be verified for load/playback/listening before being wired to the server's hit-confirmation path. No additional decorative, environment, or animation Marketplace searches are needed given the deliberately minimal scope (plain floor, default avatar, default camera). Missing integration work is limited to: parenting/positioning the dummy and its hitbox reference, extracting and playing the specific punch clip on server-approved requests, and triggering/parenting the impact sound near the dummy for server-controlled playback. All hit validation, cooldown, and counter logic are original small server-authoritative scripts/modules, since no Marketplace behavior was selected or requested for those systems.

plan.reason: The prior review flagged the embedded 'Respawn' Script (index 18) as unsafe/unsuitable behavior: it polls the dummy's own Humanoid.Health and, on death, clones and re-parents a fresh dummy while destroying the original. No replacement source or new script is added by this component; hitbox wiring and overlap math are explicitly owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task per the accepted integration task list, not by this asset-adaptation step.

removeSubtrees.reason: Embedded 'Respawn' Script implements a Humanoid-health-triggered clone/respawn loop that would make the dummy reactive to damage and eventually swap/destroy the original Model. Removing it is safe: it is a leaf Script with no descendants, and no other captured node references or depends on it.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

playerExperience.title: Punch the Dummy: Training Drill
playerExperience.summary: A minimal single-player boxing-gym practice loop. The player spawns on a plain, undecorated floor a short walk from a stationary training dummy (selected asset 1245720733), using the default Roblox avatar, default third-person camera and default WASD/gamepad movement with no arena boundaries. Pressing the single punch input (left click, Space, or gamepad A) triggers a forward jab (R15 Punching Animations asset 12061946559, clip 1/1/18/1) lasting roughly 0.3-0.5s (windup/strike/recovery) if the player is not already mid-punch. The server authoritatively checks the strike-frame overlap against the dummy's hitbox; on a confirmed hit it plays the Punch Impact 1 sound (asset 132504023010884) once and increments a persistent on-screen 'Hits: N' counter by exactly 1, gated by a per-swing hit-registered flag so only one hit registers per swing even under sustained overlap. The dummy has no health, never flinches, never attacks, and cannot be defeated or moved. There is no reset-counter control; the count persists for the session and only clears on scene reload. No combos, kicks, blocks, scoring, timers or win conditions are included. First minute: player spawns near the dummy on the plain floor, sees the 'Hits: 0' counter top-of-screen, walks up, punches, hears/see the jab animation and impact sound, and watches the counter climb with each successful connect - a simple, satisfying training-drill loop.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Bright, simple default Roblox lighting evokes a no-frills gym corner - no custom lighting rigs, fog, or moody color grading. The only authored visual elements are the imported dummy's own red-and-black canvas heavy-bag styling (asset-provided, not recolored) and a plain flat gray/neutral floor with zero decorative props or backdrop. The HUD is a single bold 'Hits: N' text label anchored to a fixed screen corner (top-center or top-right), styled like a simple arcade rep-counter (bold sans numerals, high-contrast color against a small translucent backing frame) but otherwise unadorned - no meters, health bars, or damage numbers. Player and dummy appearance come entirely from the default Roblox avatar and the selected dummy asset; no custom clothing, rig edits, or added accessories. Camera is the untouched default third-person follow camera.

plan.reason: The prior review flagged the embedded 'Respawn' Script (index 18) as unsafe/unsuitable behavior: it polls the dummy's own Humanoid.Health and, on death, clones and re-parents a fresh dummy while destroying the original. This directly conflicts with r_dummy_stationary's requirement that the dummy 'cannot be damaged, destroyed, or knocked over' and shows no reactive behavior, and it is unrelated to any requested mechanic. This manifest removes only that Script subtree, preserving every other node: the Model hierarchy, its Parts, SpecialMesh geometry, Head, Torso, the Torso's Decal (rbxassetid://406436910 canvas heavy-bag texture), and the Humanoid component itself, which remains present but will never be driven by any damage-dealing logic elsewhere in this namespace. No replacement source or new script is added by this component; hitbox wiring and overlap math are explicitly owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task per the accepted integration task list, not by this asset-adaptation step.

removeSubtrees.reason: Embedded 'Respawn' Script implements a Humanoid-health-triggered clone/respawn loop that would make the dummy reactive to damage and eventually swap/destroy the original Model. This conflicts with r_dummy_stationary's explicit acceptance criteria (no health depletion, no reactive/respawn behavior, cannot be defeated) and has no requested role in this minimal training-drill scope. Removing it is safe: it is a leaf Script with no descendants, and no other captured node references or depends on it.

preservedBehavior: Model hierarchy (index 1-2) and all body Parts (indices 3,5,7,9,10,11,12) with their SpecialMesh geometry (indices 4,6,8) retained unchanged, preserving the dummy's red/black canvas heavy-bag visual shape.
Head (index 13) and its SpecialMesh (index 14) retained unchanged.
Torso (index 15) retained unchanged as the distinguishable body part designated for later hitbox use by the separate hitDetectionModule task.
Torso Decal (index 16) with Texture rbxassetid://406436910 retained unchanged, preserving the dummy's existing canvas heavy-bag appearance required by r_theme_gym.

Humanoid (index 17) retained on the Model; it remains present as part of the asset's original rig but is not wired to any damage source in this namespace, so it will not deplete or trigger reactive behavior now that the Respawn watcher script is removed.
All joints/welds implicit in the original Part hierarchy are left intact since no geometry-bearing node was altered or removed.
remainingIntegration: Placement of this dummy Model at the fixed world position/CFrame specified for the practice-dummy target is owned by the worldSetup/dummyAssetIntegration tasks, not this component-level edit.

Designating Torso (index 15) as the authoritative server-side hitbox reference and implementing the strike-window overlap/distance math is owned by the separate hitDetectionModule task; no hitbox-defining code exists in this captured component.

Ensuring no other script anywhere in the namespace ever calls TakeDamage/sets Health on this dummy's Humanoid must be verified during integration of PunchServer and HitDetectionModule, since the Humanoid component itself was preserved rather than removed.
Visual/theme acceptance of the decal texture and mesh geometry against r_theme_gym still requires native rendering verification once the dummy is placed in the scene; this was not performed here.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end
